stem: An adolescent with diabetes is unwell at home, their glucose is low and blood ketones are elevated; what is the best response?

options.text: Give water only and withhold insulin
Stop all oral intake until ketones normalise
Treat only the ketones and ignore the glucose

explanation: Give insulin and carbohydrates. Low glucose with elevated ketones still requires insulin, and carbohydrate is needed to treat the hypoglycaemia.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

rationale: Low glucose with elevated ketones still requires insulin; carbohydrate is also needed when hypoglycaemia is present; paired glucose-ketone interpretation is essential in sick day management.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because low glucose with elevated ketones requires both insulin and carbohydrate, rather than withholding treatment.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because withholding insulin does not address ketonaemia and water alone does not treat hypoglycaemia.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because stopping all oral intake is not the recommended response when carbohydrate is needed for low glucose.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because management must address both the glucose and the ketones, not one in isolation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because this situation needs prompt active management rather than waiting until the next day.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
